A.explanation: This describes weight, $W = mg$, which is a force in newtons and depends on gravitational field strength.

B.explanation: Momentum is $p = mv$ and depends on velocity as well as mass, so it does not define mass alone.

C.explanation: Mass is a measure of inertia, so a larger mass needs a larger force to produce the same acceleration.

D.explanation: A balance compares masses, but weight is the gravitational force on the object, not the mass itself.

hints: Notice the question asks for mass, measured in $\text{kg}$, not weight measured in $\text{N}$.
Recall how mass appears in $F = ma$ as the link between applied force and resulting acceleration.
Compare an object at rest with one moving: momentum needs velocity, but resistance to acceleration depends on mass alone.
walkthrough: Identify what is asked: the meaning of mass as a property of the object itself, independent of where it is.
Recall Newton's second law $F = ma$, which can be written $m = F/a$.
This shows mass determines how much acceleration results from a given force, which is inertia or resistance to change in motion.
Weight and gravitational force depend on $g$, and momentum depends on velocity $v$, so they cannot define mass.
